editorial:
Imagine waking up in a locked room with no windows, no explanation, and no idea how long you'll be there. That's the nightmare facing Joe Doucett, a man who spends twenty years in solitary confinement before being suddenly released with just three and a half days to figure out who did this to him and why. Josh Brolin carries the film with a raw, desperate energy, while Samuel L. Jackson and Sharlto Copley add memorable turns as the people pulling the strings. The story pulls you in fast and keeps you guessing, mixing brutal action with a dark mystery that gets stranger the deeper you go.

The pacing is mostly tight, though some scenes feel stretched and the tone swings between gritty thriller and over-the-top drama. The action hits hard and the central mystery is genuinely gripping, but the remake never quite matches the shock of the original Korean film. If you enjoy dark revenge stories with a twisted payoff, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Joe discovers that Marie, the young woman he fell in love with, is actually his own daughter. Adrian Pryce reveals he orchestrated Joe's imprisonment and their romance as revenge for a rumor Joe spread years ago that led to Adrian's sister's suicide. Adrian also admits to an incestuous relationship with his sister before killing himself. Joe, unable to live with the truth, visits a hypnotist to erase his memories, but the ending stays ambiguous about whether it worked, as Marie welcomes him home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark revenge thrillers with shocking twists.
